claim: For the Yang–Chen flow \(\dot x=a(y-x)\), \(\dot y=x(c-z)\), \(\dot z=xy-bz\) with \(a,b,c>0\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure \(\mu\) satisfies \(\int x^2\,d\mu=b\bar z\), \(\int z^2\,d\mu=c\bar z\), and \(\operatorname{Var}_\mu(z)=\bar z(c-\bar z)\), where \(\bar z=\int z\,d\mu\). Thus \(0\le\bar z\le c\); the lower endpoint is only the origin measure and the upper endpoint is supported on the two outer equilibria. Consequently every non-equilibrium ergodic compact invariant measure has \(0<\bar z<c\), \(\int x^2\,d\mu<bc\), positive height variance, and positive mass both in \(0<z<c\) and in \(z<0\) or \(z>c\). In particular, any nonconstant periodic orbit with \(z(t)>0\) for all \(t\) visits both \(0<z<c\) and \(z>c\).
limitations: The theorem concerns compact invariant probability measures only; it does not prove existence, physicality, uniqueness, or stability of recurrent sets. The sign-balance theorem does not choose which outer side of the height slab is visited. Some older related literature was available only through abstract or opening material, leaving a bounded residual bibliographic risk.
scientific_integrity: All displayed identities are derived from invariant averages of explicit Lie derivatives. Endpoint rigidity is proved from invariant-support geometry. No numerical experiment is used as proof.
title: Exact stationary height parabola and slab-crossing law for the Yang–Chen flow
